content:
Update (US Eastern Time 11pm): Apple's system status page shows all issues have been resolved. The original report follows.

Just a week apart, Apple has once again experienced a major service outage affecting regular users and developers. Details below.

According to Apple's system status page, the following services are experiencing partial outages:

  • App Store: Some users affected. Users may be unable to make purchases in the iTunes Store, Mac App Store, and App Store.
  • AppleCare on Device: All users affected. AppleCare purchasing services are temporarily unavailable.
  • iTunes Store: Some users affected. Users may be unable to make purchases in the iTunes Store, Mac App Store, and App Store.
  • Mac App Store: Some users affected. Users may be unable to make purchases in the iTunes Store, Mac App Store, and App Store.
  • Subscription Purchases: Some users affected. Users may intermittently experience issues with this service.

All issues began at 7:40pm US Eastern Time and have not yet been resolved. In addition, Apple's developer system status page lists two ongoing issues that began at 7:20pm:

  • App Store – Advanced Commerce API: Some users affected. Affected services: App Store – Advanced Commerce API, App Store – In-App Purchases. We are performing emergency maintenance to improve system performance, expected to take approximately two hours.
  • App Store – In-App Purchases: Some users affected. Affected services: App Store – Advanced Commerce API, App Store – In-App Purchases. We are performing emergency maintenance to improve system performance, expected to take approximately two hours.

Although Apple has stated that the emergency maintenance affecting developer services is expected to take approximately two hours, it has not yet provided an estimated time to resolve the outage affecting users.

This report will be updated when more information becomes available.
